newsitem.title: GERMANY: Uncertain German stocks flirt with new records.
newsitem.headline: Uncertain German stocks flirt with new records.

text.p: Positive market signals and a smattering of good corporate news sent German shares to new records on Thursday, but dealings were marked by selective buying interest and weak volumes.
The 30-share DAX index continued its bull run to end the floor session up 7.58 at 2,666.55 points, after setting a new alltime intraday high of 2,672.59.
The dollar's rise above 1.52 marks boosted sentiment as did firm Bunds, but dealers were wary about the equity market's potential for further gains.
The IBIS DAX index, which tracks all-day electronic trade, slipped marginally off the day's highs in the afternoon to close at 2,664.96, almost flat on the day.
"People are getting cold feet now. I think we need some breathing space here. We really have been shooting up too fast," said a Frankfurt dealer.
Buying interest was extremely selective, dealers said.

Pharmaceuticals group Schering's announcement that it might pay a higher-than-expected two-mark dividend in 1996 helped its shares move 2.05 marks higher to 119.15, while Bayer and Hoechst also edged higher in the chemical sector.
Schering pared its gains to close IBIS trade at 118.40 marks, still up 1.25 marks.
Several banks were trading lower after Moody's Investors Service said it planned to review its ratings of the largest commercial bank in the sector, Deutsche Bank.

Deutsche shares slipped 70 pfennigs to 72.13 in bourse trade and ended at 72.10, while Commerzbank and Dresdner Bank were also lower. "The Moody's news went through the whole sector to some degree," one trader said.
ABN said it saw as more "durable" recent gains in the steel, chemical and car sector compared to those seen by banking stocks, which it said had been mainly based on takeover speculation.

Engineering group Mannesmann gained 5.50 marks to 576 marks in bourse trade, ending late trade at 573.90, on news it would be part of a French telecom consortium including Compagnie Generale des Eaux and British Telecom.
